This isn't a scene from a film. This is a heartbreaking reality that still exists in parts of Nepal. For some women and girls, getting their period means being sent away from their own home to spend the night in a small shed, away from their families. They are left to face cold nights, fear, loneliness, and the danger of snakes, insects, and wild animals—all because of a natural biological process. Menstruation should never be a reason for exclusion or shame. Take a moment and ask yourself: If it were someone you love—your daughter, your sister, your wife, or your mother—would you accept this as "tradition"? Some customs deserve to be questioned, especially when they put lives and dignity at risk. Every woman deserves to feel safe, respected, and valued, no matter what day of the month it is. Let's raise awareness, start conversations, and stand together to end harmful practices like this. Why Is Nepal’s Young Generation Leaving the Country? It’s not just about earning more money abroad — it’s about wanting a better quality of life. In Nepal, even basic tasks like getting a passport, renewing a license, or dealing with government offices can become stressful and time-consuming. Poor roads, complicated procedures, and inefficient public services add to the frustration. Meanwhile, many young people look abroad for systems that work, services they can rely on, and a life with less unnecessary stress. The private sector can create jobs and drive innovation, but public services like roads, passports, and licenses are responsibilities the government must deliver effectively. 🔥 If Nepal wants its youth to stay, it must offer more than opportunities — it must build a system where living and working here feels worthwhile. The question isn’t just why our youth are leaving. It’s what we’re doing to give them a reason to stay. #Nepal #BrainDrain #YouthMigration #NepalEconomy #GovernmentReform #PublicServices #NepaliYouth #DigitalNepal #NepalBusiness #DreamBusiness
